4. A native obstruction to forcing the early phase into small quantum clusters

The positive CP-return idea has a structural limit in the native early-time model.

Harley–König construct a constant-depth, nearest-neighbour two-dimensional Clifford preparation whose bulk single-site measurements localize a Bell pair across arbitrarily large distance, up to a computable Pauli correction. Their result tolerates a constant local-stochastic Pauli-noise strength. arxiv.org <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.05870?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

I derived a transfer to the present native model for one sufficiently large fixed rational $g$, with $\eta=0$.

Each constant-size Clifford gate is compiled into bounded-strength, finite-duration Pauli Hamiltonian rotations. Independent Pauli dressing seeds are chosen in advance. The native replacement bath remains active during every gate, dressing pulse and idle.

For the ideal-pulse reference, averaging over these seeds produces a Pauli-stochastic error channel around the intended Clifford gate. Its block error probability is $O(1/g)$; the resulting local-stochastic wire parameter is $O(g^{-1/2})$, up to fixed compilation constants. Choosing one sufficiently large fixed $g$ puts it below the source threshold.

The reference Clifford pulse times involve $\pi$. The actual native schedules use rational approximations. A paid Duhamel estimate makes the whole-state error any chosen fixed $\nu>0$ with $O(\log N+\log(1/\nu))$ timing bits. Thus the rational native family retains constant corrected Bell fidelity, for example above $0.9$.

This yields an efficiently generated randomized family and existence of fixed schedules with that fidelity. It does not identify a particular good seed deterministically.

Now suppose a positive quantum-state decomposition assigns probability $\theta$ to components whose quantum cluster joins the two distant endpoints. In all other components, local bulk measurements and a final local Pauli-frame correction leave a separable endpoint state, whose Bell fidelity is at most $1/2$. Consequently,
$F_{\mathrm{Bell}}\le \frac12+\frac{\theta}{2}.$
Constant fidelity above $0.9$ forces substantial spanning-cluster probability. A uniformly exponentially small probability of such a cluster cannot describe every early native schedule.
